name: Micron Hiroshima cleanroom expansion

parties.name: Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry (Japan)
parties.note: Decided in September 2025 to subsidize the production expansion at the Hiroshima plant.

process_nodes.label: 1-gamma (1γ) DRAM
process_nodes.note: Trade press links the expansion to scaling 1-gamma DRAM output; Micron's filing does not name a node.

summary: A new cleanroom project at Micron's existing DRAM fab in Hiroshima, Japan, aimed at advanced DRAM and HBM for AI systems. Japan's industry ministry agreed in September 2025 to subsidize roughly a third of a planned 1.5 trillion yen investment. Micron broke ground in July 2026; equipment installation is due to begin in the second half of 2028 and the company expects initial output in late calendar 2028.

location.note: At Micron's existing Hiroshima manufacturing facility.

metrics.note: Planned through the end of fiscal 2029, according to the 2025 subsidy reporting.
Capital spending subsidy; the 2025 reporting adds up to 36 billion yen over five years for related R&D, for a total of up to 536 billion yen.
Peak capacity target for early 2030 in wafers per month; the source does not state the wafer size.

milestones.note: The plan became public when the industry ministry announced its subsidy.
Micron expects initial output in late calendar 2028; the 2025 reporting targeted shipments around mid-2028.

sources.title: Micron Technology, Inc. Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended September 3, 2026
[News] Micron Breaks Ground on Hiroshima Fab Expansion, Scaling 1γ DRAM and HBM Output as Equipment Set for 2H28
Japan grants $3.6 bln to Micron for advanced memory expansion in Hiroshima

notes: Micron has not named the new cleanroom building, so it is recorded as a project at the Hiroshima site. Reported subsidy totals differ between 500 billion yen (capital spending only) and 536 billion yen (including R&D support).

review.method: Independent AI-assisted review (Claude): re-opened every cited source, checked each statement against it and searched for newer reporting.
review.changes: Set the investment and capacity qualifiers to exact, as both sources state the figures without approximation, and dated the investment figure to the July 2026 report.
